name: com.cuvara.dots
description: Shared DOTS/ECS building blocks for Cuvara projects — reusable components, systems, jobs and authoring helpers built on Unity Entities, Burst, Collections and Mathematics.

samples.description: Ready-to-play scene. Entities drive pooled GameObject views: DotsViewBootstrap.Install, a self-contained IViewAssetProvider over Unity primitives, orbiting entities so transform sync is visible, despawn/recycle, and a narrated chunk warm/release showing a shared key surviving one chunk's release. Needs neither VContainer nor GameFoundation nor Addressables.

Drives the netcode adapter and the prediction driver end to end against a running backend. Replicated entities become ECS entities with pooled primitive views; the local player is client-side predicted. An on-screen overlay shows what the server sent beside where it was drawn, and which of the two writers owns the local transform.

Pure DOTS and hybrid entity stress benchmark. Measures simulation + Unity.Physics throughput at 100 to 100M entities. Two modes: pure ECS (no views) and hybrid (pooled GameObjects). Command-line activated via -stress-pure or -stress-hybrid.

No server, no network. A scripted DotsEntityView is driven with the same IEntityView/IEntityPoseView calls the binder makes against a live connection, and everything downstream is the production path: the drain, EntityPose, the NetworkGameEvent buffer and EntityPoseViewSystem. Two buttons carry the argument. 'Stop sending action_seq': the attacker keeps attacking, the readout still says action=Attacking every frame, and the swing counter FREEZES -- because action is level-triggered, two swings in a row are the same value, and no client-side cleverness recovers an edge that is not in the data. 'Stop sending events': the victim's health keeps falling and the damage log stops, because HP is state and a hit is an occurrence. The consumer side is nine lines (SwingFlash): it is told the action and whether it was re-entered, and deliberately never sees the counter -- the inequality comparison and the per-entity memory are the package's job, and a view script handed the raw number gets one of them wrong.

Four offline scenes demonstrating the v0.28.0 DOTS improvement plan: pool and chunk accounting, module lifecycle and view-config validation, the scripted network entity lifecycle with minimap and overlays, and the physics event pipeline. No backend required; the netcode and physics scenes are gated on their optional packages.
